newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RTZ-CRA says metals lower than fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RTZ-CRA says metals lower than fundamentals.

text.p: Dual-listed mining giant RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd said on Thursday greater efficiencies resulting from the refocusing and restructuring of global operations are expected to show savings of US$50 million per year from 1997.

RTZ-CRA also said in a statement accompanying its half year results that current price levels of many metals appear to be more depressed than the fundamentals of supply, demand and stocks would suggest.
RTZ-CRA chief executive Robert Wilson said in a statement that first half demand for metals in the large industrial economies had been mixed.

"Western world copper consumption was over three percent higher than in the first half of 1995 but demand for some others was down on the previous year, including aluminium by almost seven percent," Wilson said.
"Overall, non-ferrous metals prices declined by 11 percent compared with the first half of 1995," he said.
CRA chairman John Uhrig said market sentiment had a sharp adverse impact on metals prices in 1996.

"Confidence was shaken by Sumitomo's announcement in June," Uhrig said. "The current price levels of many metals appear to be more depressed than the fundamentals of supply, demand and stocks would suggest," he said.
He said economic indicators pointed to a broadly based improvement in the second half of this year and stronger markets in 1997.

"On a longer-term view, we are confident about growth of demand, especially from the Asian region which now accounts for a signifciant share of global consumption of all metals and minerals," Uhrig said.
RTZ-CRA earlier reported a net profit of A$714 million for the six months to June 30 from A$735 million the previous corresponding half.
